summary: The paper builds étale motives on Berkovich spaces from scratch, uniformly for archimedean and nonarchimedean Banach rings. Banach rings carry the arc-topology (finitely many maps jointly surjective on Berkovich spectra), whose basis of strictly totally disconnected rings makes finitary functors hypercomplete arc-sheaves; D^eff_mot(X) is the category of finitary, ball-invariant arc-sheaves, and D_mot(X) inverts ℤ(1) = Ḡ_m[−1]. Main results: the cancellation theorem over any base (Theorem 1.9); rational motivic cohomology equals the Adams eigenspaces of rational K-theory, with explicit descriptions via cofib(K(A_{<1}) → K(A)) (Theorem 1.7); a six-functor formalism with smooth maps cohomologically smooth and D_mot(X) rigid dualizable for analytic X of finite cohomological dimension (Theorem 1.12); D_mot(k) is Voevodsky's étale motives for discrete algebraically closed k (Proposition 1.13); motives over C = completed k((T))^alg are pairs (A, N) over k via motivic nearby cycles (Theorem 1.14); torsion motives are overconvergent étale sheaves on v-stacks (§12). The atlas has a pending Part II of MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles for rigid-analytic motives (from Binda–Kato–Vezzani) carrying the same tilting, good-reduction and nearby-cycles theorems for Ayoub's RigDA, so the Berkovich construction coalesces with it; Banach rings go to TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0–TB.1, K-theory inputs to GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.5, SchemeKTheoryOperations S.3/S.5 and RefinedTraceMethods RT.5, dualizable and rigid categories to EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5. Three misprints are recorded.

items.name: Seminormed rings and Banach rings (Scholze's conventions)
items.statement: A seminormed ring is a commutative unital ring R with |·|_R : R → ℝ_{≥0} such that |0| = 0, |−1| ≤ 1, |xy| ≤ |x||y| and |x + y| ≤ |x| + |y|; maps are norm-nonincreasing ring maps. A Banach ring is a complete seminormed ring (then |·| is a norm; R = 0 allowed since |1| = 1 is not required). Any ring with the discrete norm is a Banach ring. Seminormed and Banach rings have all colimits (pushouts via the projective tensor norm, completion; Proposition 2.4); free seminormed algebras R[T_1..T_n]_{r_1..r_n} (§2.1); power-multiplicative R is nonarchimedean iff |2| ≤ 1 (Proposition 2.6).
items.note: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0 plans the Berkovich spectrum of Banach algebras over a field; this general category of Banach rings (all Banach rings, including ℤ and archimedean ones) extends its input.

items.name: Proposition 2.9: seminormed rings form a compactly assembled category
items.statement: A map f : X → Y in a presentable ∞-category is weakly compact if every map from Y to a filtered colimit colim Z_i lifts through some Z_i after precomposing with f; C is compactly assembled if filtered colimits commute with finite limits and C is generated by sequential colimits along weakly compact maps (Definition 2.7; equivalently colim : Ind(C) → C has a left adjoint, Ramzi). The category of seminormed rings is compactly assembled — ℤ[T]_r = colim_{r′>r} ℤ[T]_{r′} along compact maps — though not compactly generated, and Banach rings are not.

items.name: Gelfand–Mazur for Banach fields
items.statement: A Banach field is a Banach ring (K, |·|) with K a field and |·| multiplicative (Definition 2.10); Banach fields are discrete, archimedean or nonarchimedean. Any Banach field with |2|_K > 1 is isomorphic to ℝ or ℂ with |·|^α for some 0 < α ≤ 1 (Theorem 2.12).
items.note: Mathlib has the core: NormedAlgebra.Real.nonempty_algEquiv_or (a normed field that is a normed ℝ-algebra is ℝ or ℂ) and NormedAlgebra.Complex.nonempty_algEquiv; the step from |2| > 1 to a normed ℝ-algebra structure with |·|^α (Ostrowski) is not there.

items.name: The Berkovich spectrum M(R) and completed residue fields
items.statement: M(R) ⊂ ∏_{r∈R} [0, |r|_R] is the compact Hausdorff space of multiplicative seminorms ‖·‖ ≤ |·|_R with ‖1‖ = 1 (Definition 2.13); for s ∈ M(R), K(s) is the completed residue Banach field, and points are equivalently maps R → K to Banach fields with dense fraction field of the image; M(R) ≠ ∅ when |1|_R = 1 (Theorem 2.14), f is invertible iff ‖f‖ > 0 on M(R) (Corollary 2.15, Wiener's theorem).
items.locator: §1, p. 2; §2.2, Definition 2.13, Theorem 2.14, Corollary 2.15, Remark 2.16, pp. 10–11
items.note: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0 plans the Berkovich spectrum of a Banach algebra from bounded multiplicative seminorms, its topology and completed residue fields.

items.name: Theorem 2.18 and §2.3: idempotents, uniform rings and the Gelfand transform
items.statement: A Banach ring is analytic if all K(x) are non-discrete (Definition 2.17, Kedlaya–Liu); idempotents of a Banach ring R correspond to open and closed subsets of M(R) (Theorem 2.18; via overconvergent rational localisations and Kedlaya–Liu [KL15, Cor. 2.8.9], or animated gaseous sheaves). The Gelfand transform R → ∏^Ban_s K(s) (Definition 2.19); R is uniform if it is isometric (Definition 2.20), iff |·| is power-multiplicative, the spectral norm being lim |xⁿ|^{1/n} (Proposition 2.21), which defines the uniform completion.
items.note: Extends TB.0's Berkovich spectrum to the Banach-ring toolkit the arc-topology needs.

items.name: §2.4: the Berkovich closed disc over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field
items.statement: M(C⟨T⟩_1) = {(x_a)_{a∈O_C} : x_a ≤ max(x_b, |a − b|), |a − b| ≤ max(x_a, x_b)} ⊂ ∏[0,1], an inverse limit of finite trees; points are of types (1)–(4) with residue fields C, the completion of C(T) with transcendental residue extension, with value group |C^×| × x_a^ℤ (C⟨(T−a)^{±1}⟩_{x_a}), or an immediate extension; types (3), (4) disappear for |C| = ℝ_{≥0}, resp. spherically complete C.
items.note: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.1 plans the four point types on the affine line, paths and skeletons. Misprint 'pm1' for ±1 (source issue E1).

items.name: The arc-topology on Banach rings and arc-stacks
items.statement: {A → B_i} is an arc-cover if for some finite J ⊂ I the map ⊔_{i∈J} M(B_i) → M(A) is surjective — equivalently every A → K to a Banach field lifts to some B_i after a field extension (Definition 3.1). M_arc(A) is the arc-sheafification of Hom(A, −); κ-small Banach rings and small arc-sheaves (small colimits of M_arc(A)'s); objects of the arc-site are qcqs (Proposition 3.3).
items.note: The Banach-ring analogue of the scheme-theoretic arc-topology of Bhatt–Mathew (the proposed ArcTopologyAndDescent roadmap, which is for qcqs schemes) and of the v-topology on perfectoid spaces (DiamondsAndVStacks).

items.name: Proposition 3.2: Berkovich spectra of pushouts and filtered colimits
items.statement: For a pushout D = B ⊗_A C of seminormed rings, M(D) → M(B) ×_{M(A)} M(C) is surjective; for a filtered colimit A = colim A_i, M(A) ≅ lim M(A_i).
items.note: Proof: reduce to Banach fields and |1|_D = 1 via integral models or Laurent series.

items.name: Examples 3.4–3.8 and Proposition 3.9: basic arc-covers
items.statement: A → completion of A[T^{±1}]_{1/2} (locally analytic); A → its uniform completion; A → ∏^Ban_{x∈M(A)} K(x); in characteristic p, A → A_perf (so sheafification perfects); over ℂ, A → Cont(M(A), ℂ) — so the arc-site on Banach ℂ-algebras is Morita equivalent to compact Hausdorff spaces with finite jointly surjective covers (condensed sets), and over ℝ to compact Hausdorff spaces with involution.
items.note: Example 3.6 calls the target totally disconnected, which needs A analytic (source issue E3).

items.name: Proposition 3.11 to Theorem 3.14: strictly totally disconnected Banach rings
items.statement: A Banach ring is totally disconnected if analytic, uniform and M(A) profinite, strictly so if moreover every K(x) is algebraically closed (Definition 3.10); ∏^Ban K_i of non-discrete (algebraically closed) fields is (strictly) totally disconnected with M = β(I) and residue fields Banach ultraproducts (Proposition 3.11); these form a basis (Corollary 3.12) on which the arc-topology is subcanonical (Theorem 3.13); on perfectoid Banach rings with |p| < 1 it is subcanonical too (Theorem 3.14; overconvergent v-sheaves).
items.locator: §1, Definition 1.3, p. 3; §3, Definition 3.10, Proposition 3.11, Corollary 3.12, Theorems 3.13, 3.14, pp. 16–18
items.note: Parallel to strictly totally disconnected perfectoid spaces in DiamondsAndVStacks.

items.name: Theorem 4.1: finitary functors are hypercomplete arc-sheaves
items.statement: For any Banach ring A, a functor F from strictly totally disconnected Banach A-algebras to anima commuting with finite products and filtered colimits is a hypercomplete arc-sheaf; for abelian-group valued F, its cohomology on strictly totally disconnected B vanishes in positive degrees. The same holds for compactly generated or compactly assembled targets (Remark 4.2).
items.note: Proof via quasi-pro-étale covers (Definition 4.3, Lemmas 4.4–4.7) and splitting of arc-covers of strictly totally disconnected rings (Lemmas 4.8–4.9).

items.name: Lemmas 4.4–4.9: quasi-pro-étale covers and splittings
items.statement: A → B is quasi-pro-étale if after base change to any algebraically closed Banach field C the uniform completion of B ⊗_A C is Cont(S, C) for a profinite S (Definition 4.3); analytic A has a quasi-pro-étale strictly totally disconnected cover (Lemma 4.4); over strictly totally disconnected A these are profinite sets over M(A) (Lemma 4.5), whose sheaves are sheaves on M(A) (Lemma 4.6); n-truncated finitary functors extend by quasi-pro-étale sheafification keeping finitariness (Lemma 4.7); arc-covers of strictly totally disconnected A are completed filtered colimits of split ones (Lemma 4.8), since open U ⊂ 𝔸ⁿ_A surjecting onto M(A) has a section (Lemma 4.9).

items.name: Finitary arc-sheaves D_fin(X, ℤ)
items.statement: For a small arc-stack X, D_fin(X, ℤ) ⊂ D(X_arc, ℤ) is the full subcategory of arc-sheaves whose restriction to strictly totally disconnected Banach rings over X commutes with filtered colimits (Definition 4.10); equivalently functors from strictly totally disconnected rings over X to D(ℤ) commuting with finite products and filtered colimits (Proposition 4.12); it is stable under colimits and truncations and left-complete (Proposition 4.13); for D⁺ commutation holds on all Banach rings (Remark 4.11).

items.name: Theorem 4.14 and Propositions 4.15–4.16: finitary sheaves over ℂ, at points and on M(A)
items.statement: For a Banach ℂ-algebra A, pullback identifies the left-complete derived category of sheaves on M(A) with D_fin(M_arc(A), ℤ) (Theorem 4.14). For a non-discrete Banach field K with completed algebraic closure C, M(K) ≅ M(C)^{hG_K} (continuous, i.e. condensed, group cohomology; Proposition 4.15); for M ∈ D⁺_fin(M_arc(A)), Rν_*M on M(A) has stalks M(K(x)) (Proposition 4.16). Cohomological dimension d(X) (Definition 4.17) is bounded by dim M(A) + sup cd G_{K(x)} (Corollary 4.18).

items.name: Theorem 4.20: proper base change for finitary sheaves
items.statement: Proper maps are 0-truncated qcqs maps of small arc-stacks, with cohomological dimension d(f) (Definition 4.19). For f proper of finite cohomological dimension, f_* preserves finitary sheaves with finite cohomological dimension and commutes with any base change; for f quasi-pro-étale it satisfies the projection formula. Example 4.26: the projection formula fails for P¹_X → X (the sheaf Ḡ_m has H¹(P¹_C, Ḡ_m) ≠ 0).
items.note: Uses repleteness of the arc-topos and Postnikov completeness (Mondal–Reinecke [MR25]).

items.name: Definitions 4.21–4.22, Lemma 4.23, Propositions 4.24–4.25: open immersions, finitary maps, excision
items.statement: Open immersions are representable by open subspaces of M(A) (Definition 4.21); f is finitary if Y(A) commutes with filtered colimits of strictly totally disconnected rings relative to X (Definition 4.22); finitary maps are stable under composition, pullback and cancellation, colimits, include open immersions and finitary injections are open immersions (Lemma 4.23); for finitary f, f_♯ preserves finitary sheaves with the projection formula (Proposition 4.24); j_!j^*M → M → i_*i^*M is exact for finitary M (Proposition 4.25), separating the archimedean locus |2| > 1 from the nonarchimedean locus.

items.name: Effective motivic sheaves D^eff_mot(X)
items.statement: Y is ball-invariant if Y(A) → Y(A⟨T⟩_1) is an isomorphism for all Banach rings A over X (Definition 5.1). D^eff_mot(X) ⊂ D_fin(X, ℤ) is the full subcategory of ball-invariant finitary arc-sheaves ('étale motives' with ℤ-coefficients; the sphere spectrum would work equally, Definition 5.2 and footnote 3).
items.note: The Berkovich analogue of Ayoub's rigid-analytic motives RigDA (the coalesced Part II's rigid-motive layer) and of Voevodsky's étale motives.

items.name: Lemma 5.3, Corollaries 5.4–5.5, Propositions 5.6–5.8: the ball-localisation L_B
items.statement: C⟨T⟩_1 has cohomological dimension ≤ 3 (Lemma 5.3); ball-invariance can be checked on algebraically closed fields (Corollary 5.4); D^eff_mot is closed under colimits (Corollary 5.5); the left adjoint is L_B(M)(A) = colim_{[n]∈Δ^op} M(A⟨Δⁿ⟩) with Δⁿ = 𝔹ⁿ (Proposition 5.6, via Lurie HTT 5.2.7.4; the presheaf version L_B^pre, Remark 5.7); L_B is a Verdier quotient by the ⊗-ideal of 𝔹-contractible sheaves, giving a unique symmetric monoidal structure (Proposition 5.8, Nikolaus–Scholze Theorem I.3.6).

items.name: Proposition 5.9 and Corollary 6.6: torsion motives are étale sheaves
items.statement: For n with |n| ≥ 1 on X, a finitary ℤ/n-sheaf invariant under change of algebraically closed field is ball-invariant (Proposition 5.9, via Berkovich [Ber93, Thms 6.3.9, 6.4.1] or an explicit Kummer computation on trees); conversely ball-invariant ℤ/n-sheaves are invariant under change of algebraically closed field (Corollary 6.6).
items.locator: §1, Proposition 1.5(ii), p. 4; §5, Proposition 5.9, pp. 28–30; §6, Corollary 6.6, p. 39

items.name: Proposition 5.10 and Corollary 6.9: the homotopy t-structure
items.statement: D^eff_mot(X, ℚ) ⊂ D_fin(X, ℚ) is stable under truncations (C⟨T⟩_1 has cohomological dimension 1 rationally; Proposition 5.10), and so is D^eff_mot(X) ⊂ D_fin(X, ℤ) (Corollary 6.9); the Tate twist sits in degree −1.

items.name: Lemma 5.11 to Theorem 5.14: free motivic sheaves and f_♯
items.statement: For open U ⊂ 𝔸ⁿ_X, L_B^pre(U) is finitary (Lemma 5.11); so the free motivic sheaf ℤ_mot[U] ∈ D^eff_mot(X) exists, represents M ↦ M(U), commutes with base change and takes fibre products to tensor products (Proposition 5.12); for X = M_arc(A) analytic of finite cohomological dimension these generate D^eff_mot(X) (Proposition 5.13); for f : Y → 𝔸ⁿ_X → X (finitary then projection), f^* has a left adjoint f_♯ with base change and projection formula (Theorem 5.14).

items.name: Theorem 5.16 and Proposition 5.17 (= Proposition 1.6): the reduced multiplicative group
items.statement: On the nonarchimedean locus, Ḡ_m := G_m/(1 + O_{<1}) is finitary and ball-invariant (Theorem 5.16; modulo ℓ via Proposition 5.9, rationally via Pic(C⟨T⟩_1) = 0 and harmonicity of norm functions on trees), and ℤ_mot[G_m]/ℤ_mot[∗] ≅ Ḡ_m via characteristic polynomials Symⁿ(Ḡ_m) ≅ 𝔸^{n−1} × Ḡ_m (Proposition 5.17).
items.locator: §1, Proposition 1.6, p. 5; §5.2, Definition 5.15, Theorem 5.16, Proposition 5.17, pp. 32–34

items.name: The Tate twist ℤ(1) and Proposition 5.19
items.statement: ℤ(1) := (ℤ_mot[G_m]/ℤ_mot[∗])[−1] (Definition 5.18); over ℂ it is ℤ, over ℝ with complex conjugation acting nontrivially, and on the nonarchimedean locus ℤ(1) ≅ Ḡ_m[−1]. Over strictly totally disconnected X, ℤ(1) is compact and ℤ_mot[T] ≅ ℤ_mot[G_m] for every open annulus T (Proposition 5.19, via Newton polygons: Symⁿ(T) → T(r_1ⁿ, r_2ⁿ) is a fibration in open balls).

items.name: Theorem 6.1: explicit free motivic sheaves
items.statement: For a finitary arc-sheaf of sets U over X and strictly totally disconnected A over X, after inverting all primes p with |p| < 1 somewhere on M(A), ℤ_mot[U](A) is the group completion of L_B^pre(ℕ[U])(A); rationally this also holds on affine subsets of 𝔸¹_A; modulo n with |n| ≥ 1, ℤ_mot[U]/n is invariant under change of algebraically closed field.

items.name: Definition 6.2 and Theorem 6.3: presheaves with transfer
items.statement: Over strictly totally disconnected X, presheaves of abelian groups with transfer are additive functors on the category whose maps A → B are maps ℕ[M_arc(A)/X] → ℕ[M_arc(B)/X] of arc-sheaves of commutative monoids (Definition 6.2). For a finitary ball-invariant such M, the derived arc-sheafification is ball-invariant after inverting primes with |p| < 1 somewhere, invariant under change of algebraically closed field mod n, and M ⊗ ℚ is already a sheaf on open subsets of 𝔸¹_A with unchanged values on affine subsets (Theorem 6.3).
items.note: The analogue of Voevodsky's presheaves with transfers (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5a plans the algebraic theory).

items.name: Lemmas 6.4–6.5: homotopies on curves and motives of domains in the line
items.statement: For a smooth connected curve U over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean C and a prime p, any two points x, x′ ∈ U(C) satisfy x + p x_1 + … + p x_n ~_𝔹 x′ + p x′_1 + … + p x′_n in ℕ[U] for suitable points (Lemma 6.4; divisibility of the generalised Jacobian with trivialisations on boundary discs, van der Put [vdP80]). For U, V ⊂ 𝔸¹_C with complements finite unions of closed discs, ℚ_mot[U] ≅ ℚ ⊕ Ḡ_m^d and its value on V is the cokernel of ℕ[U](V × 𝔹) ⊗ ℚ → ℕ[U](V) ⊗ ℚ, in degree 0 (Lemma 6.5).
items.note: Misprint P¹_A for P¹_C in Lemma 6.5 and the proof of Theorem 6.3 (source issue E2).

items.name: Theorem 6.7 and Proposition 6.8: p-torsion and tilting
items.statement: If |p|_A < 1 then p is invertible in D^eff_mot(M(A)) (after tilting, Artin–Schreier 0 → 𝔽_p → 𝔹 → 𝔹 → 0); if |p| ≥ 1 on M(A), the p-power torsion part of D^eff_mot(M(A)) is the left-completed derived category of p-power torsion étale sheaves (Theorem 6.7). For X with |p| < 1 everywhere, tilting gives D^eff_mot(X) ≅ D^eff_mot(X^♭), both ℤ[1/p]-linear (Proposition 6.8; Vezzani's motivic Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem [Vez19]).
items.note: The coalesced Part II already carries the motivic Fontaine–Wintenberger equivalence for RigDA (from the Binda–Kato–Vezzani extraction).

items.name: Theorem 7.1 (= Theorem 1.9): the cancellation theorem over any base
items.statement: For any small arc-stack X, − ⊗ ℤ(1) : D^eff_mot(X) → D^eff_mot(X) is fully faithful. Unlike the algebraic and rigid-analytic settings (where it holds only over fields), it holds over any base, reducing formally to geometric points (Remarks 1.10, 7.2).
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.9, Remark 1.10, p. 6; §7, Theorem 7.1, Remark 7.2, pp. 40–43
items.note: After Voevodsky [Voe10]; Ayoub proved it for rigid-analytic motives with transfers and Vezzani showed transfers do not matter [Vez17]. Proof: rationally over C, a splitting of ℚ_mot[U] → Hom(ℚ_mot[(Ḡ_m, ∗)], ℚ_mot[U × (Ḡ_m, ∗)]) on π_i built from the loci Y_1 (balls around N-th roots of unity) and Y_2 = {p_1^N = p_2}.

items.name: Lemma 7.3: the symmetric group acts trivially on ℤ(1)^{⊗n}
items.statement: For σ ∈ Σ_n the action of σ on ℤ(1)^{⊗n} is trivial (reduce to the swap on ℤ(2)[3] = reduced homology of 𝔸² ∖ {0}, where SL_2 acts trivially by homotopy invariance and −1 acts trivially on Ḡ_m); after cancellation the action is homotopy-coherently trivial.

items.name: Corollaries 8.1–8.2: symmetric powers and ℚ_mot[∗/G_m]
items.statement: Symⁿ(ℚ(1)) = ℚ(n); ℚ_mot[∗/G_m] = ⊕_{n≥0} ℚ(n)[2n], with ℚ_mot[Pⁿ] → ℚ_mot[∗/G_m] (classifying O(1)) an isomorphism onto ⊕_{i≤n} ℚ(i)[2i]; the cofibre of ℤ_mot[P^{n−1}] → ℤ_mot[Pⁿ] is ℤ(n)[2n].

items.name: Propositions 8.4–8.5 and Corollary 8.6 (= Theorem 1.7(i)–(ii)): K-theory and motivic cohomology
items.statement: Let K^cn(A) be the connective K-theory of the abstract ring A (group completion of the E_∞-monoid of finite projective modules; Definition 8.3). Its universal ball-invariant arc-sheaf 𝒦 is finitary and an E_∞-ring (Proposition 8.4, Breen–Deligne resolutions [Aok24, Thm 4.4]); ℚ_mot[∗/G_m] ≅ 𝒦 ⊗ ℚ via line bundles (Proposition 8.5: ℚ_mot[∗/(G_mⁿ ⋊ Σ_n)] ≅ ℚ_mot[∗/GL_n] by the Σ_n-invariants of the flag variety and cancellation); hence 𝒦 ⊗ ℚ ≅ ⊕_{n≥0} ℚ(n)[2n], a filtration split canonically by Adams operations (Corollary 8.6).
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.7(i), (ii), Remark 1.8, p. 5; §8, Definition 8.3, Propositions 8.4, 8.5, Corollary 8.6, pp. 44–46
items.note: The paper notes the argument also works in classical motivic homotopy theory.

items.name: Adams operations and eigenspaces on rational K-theory
items.statement: Adams operations ψ^k act on rational K-theory with ψ^k = k^j on the weight-j eigenspace, giving the Adams decomposition used to identify rational motivic cohomology with Adams eigenspaces.
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.7(ii), p. 5; §8, Corollary 8.6, p. 46; §11, Theorem 11.1, p. 57 (used)
items.note: SchemeKTheoryOperations S.6 plans λ- and Adams operations and the eigenvalue ψ^k = k^j on weight-j rational K-theory.

items.name: Propositions 8.7–8.8 and Theorem 8.9 (= Theorem 1.7(iii)–(iv)): K-theory of the 1-units
items.statement: With a unit T, |T| < 1, having n-th roots for infinitely many n, A_{<1} is Tor-unital and K(A_{<1}) is the K-theory of the dualizable category of almost modules. The universal ball-invariant arc-sheaf under A ↦ K^cn(A_{<1}) is trivial (Proposition 8.7); A ↦ cofib(K(A_{<1}) → K(A)) commutes with filtered colimits (Proposition 8.8); on strictly totally disconnected A with |p| ≥ 1 for p ∉ S, cofib(K(A_{<1}) → K(A))[1/S] is a finitary ball-invariant arc-sheaf, hence equals 𝒦[1/S] (Theorem 8.9). So 𝒦(C) ≅ cofib(K(C_{<1}) → K(C))[1/p] for C algebraically closed nonarchimedean of residue characteristic p, and 𝒦(A) ⊗ ℚ ≅ cofib(K(A_{<1}) → K(A)) ⊗ ℚ when A_{≤1} completes a smooth O_C-algebra.

items.name: Corollary 8.10: an E_∞-structure on the cofibre
items.statement: For C algebraically closed nonarchimedean, cofib(K(C_{<1}) → K(C)) has a natural E_∞-K(C)-algebra structure (after inverting p it is 𝒦(C); after p-completion it is K(k)^∧_p = ℤ_p, Hesselholt–Nikolaus [HN20, L1.3.7], Kratzer [Kra80, Cor. 5.5]).
items.note: The categorical reason is unclear ('almost O_C-modules form an ideal in C-vector spaces').

items.name: Theorems 8.11–8.13 and Corollary 8.12: analytic descent for the cofibre
items.statement: On perfectoid Banach rings (|p| < 1), cofib(K(A_{<1}) → K(A)) is a sheaf for the analytic topology (torsion almost modules localise on M(A); Theorem 8.11), and when all sheaves on M(A) are Postnikov complete, its rationalisation is a finitary ball-invariant hypercomplete arc-sheaf, so 𝒦(A)_ℚ = cofib(K(A_{<1}) → K(A))_ℚ (Corollary 8.12, using 𝔸¹-invariance of K over valuation rings). On all analytic nonarchimedean A, cofib(KH(A_{<1}) → KH(A)) is an analytic sheaf, giving 𝒦(A)_ℚ = cofib(KH …)_ℚ, and = cofib(K …)_ℚ for totally disconnected A (Theorem 8.13).

items.name: Suslin's excision for Tor-unital non-unital rings
items.statement: For a Tor-unital non-unital ring I (ℤ ⊗^L_{I⁺} ℤ = ℤ), K(I) := fib(K(I⁺) → K(ℤ)) agrees with fib(K(A′) → K(A′/I)) for every unital ring A′ containing I as an ideal [Sus95].
items.note: GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.5 plans relative and non-unital theories with 'excision under the hypotheses of the adopted theorem'; Suslin's theorem is that adopted theorem here.

items.name: K-theory inputs: Thomason–Trobaugh, cdh and pro-cdh descent, 𝔸¹-invariance over valuation rings
items.statement: K-theory with supports is unchanged under T-adic completion (Thomason–Trobaugh [TT90, Prop. 3.19]); KH satisfies cdh-descent (Cisinski [Cis13]); K-theory satisfies pro-cdh descent (Morrow [Mor16, Thm 3.7] in equal characteristic 0, Kerz–Strunk–Tamme [KST18, Thm A]); algebraic K-theory is 𝔸¹-invariant over valuation rings; with torsion coefficients, Gabber–Suslin rigidity under change of algebraically closed field.
items.locator: §1, p. 6; §8, proofs of Proposition 8.8, Theorems 8.9, 8.13, Corollary 8.12, pp. 47–50 (cited)
items.note: SchemeKTheoryOperations S.3 (supports and localisation) and S.5 (homotopy invariance, homotopy K-theory for singular schemes) are their owners in the atlas; these descent theorems belong there.

items.name: Efimov's K-theory of dualizable categories
items.statement: Localising invariants such as K-theory extend to dualizable presentable stable ∞-categories and send Verdier sequences to fibre sequences; the category D(B^a) of almost modules for an idempotent ideal is dualizable, so K(D(B^a)) = fib(K(B) → K(B/A_{<1})) depends only on A_{<1} [Efi24]; compact objects of a filtered colimit of dualizable categories are the colimit of compact objects [Efi24, Prop. 1.72].
items.note: RefinedTraceMethods RT.5 plans compact/dualizable objects and continuous extensions of localizing invariants (the Efimov–Scholze refinement); Efimov's K-theory of dualizable categories belongs there.

items.name: Quillen: rational K-theory of finite fields
items.statement: K(𝔽_q)_ℚ = ℚ[0] (the rational homology of finite groups vanishes, K(𝔽_q) being the group completion of ⊔ ∗/GL_n(𝔽_q)); hence K(𝔽̄_p)_ℚ = ℚ[0] and there are no nonzero rational maps between distinct Tate twists in D_mot(𝔽̄_p).
items.note: KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.1 plans Quillen's finite-field calculation.

items.name: Definition 9.1 (= Definition 1.11): motivic sheaves D_mot(X)
items.statement: D_mot(X) = D^eff_mot(X)[ℤ(1)^{⊗−1}] (Robalo [Rob15]) = colim along −⊗ℤ(1) in presentable categories = lim along Hom(ℤ(1), −); objects are sequences M_n with M_n ≅ Hom(ℤ(1), M_{n+1}), and D^eff_mot(X) ⊂ D_mot(X) is fully faithful by cancellation.

items.name: Theorem 9.2 and Proposition 9.3: pushforward and the projective line
items.statement: For f : M_arc(B) → M_arc(A) of finite cohomological dimension with Y embedded in a finite-dimensional ball over X, f_* on D_mot commutes with colimits and base change and satisfies the projection formula (Theorem 9.2); for f : P¹_X → X, f_♯ ≅ f_* ⊗ ℤ(1)[2] (Proposition 9.3; unit from the G_m-torsor O(Δ), counit from the reduced cohomology of P¹).

items.name: The six-functor formalism X ↦ D_mot(X) on small arc-stacks
items.statement: Starting from affine arc-sheaves with maps of finite cohomological dimension as !-able and proper maps, the extension theorems [Sch25b, Thm 5.19], [HM24, Thm 3.4.11] give a six-functor formalism on small arc-stacks; open immersions are !-able with j_! left adjoint to j^* (Proposition 9.4); étale maps (finitary with finite geometric fibres) are !-able and cohomologically étale (Proposition 9.5); smooth K-analytic spaces without boundary are cohomologically smooth (Corollary 9.6); proper 0-truncated maps of locally finite cohomological dimension satisfy the projection formula (Corollary 10.2).
items.locator: §1, p. 6; §9, Propositions 9.4, 9.5, Corollary 9.6, pp. 52; §10, Corollary 10.2, pp. 53–54
items.note: The abstract extension theorems of Scholze's Six-Functor Formalisms notes and Heyer–Mann are prerequisites; the atlas has six operations only for diamonds (DiamondSixOperations) and étale sheaves.

items.name: Proposition 9.7: tilting for D_mot
items.statement: For X with |p| < 1 and tilt X^♭, tilting gives a symmetric monoidal equivalence D_mot(X) ≅ D_mot(X^♭), functorial in X.
items.note: From Proposition 6.8, since the Tate twist is preserved.

items.name: Proposition 10.1 (= Theorem 1.12, geometric points)
items.statement: For an algebraically closed Banach field C, D_mot(C) is compactly generated with compact unit and compact = dualizable objects, hence rigid; in equal characteristic with a splitting k → C of the residue field, it is generated by ℤ_mot[X_C](−j) for X smooth projective over k and j ≥ 0 (motives of smooth projective varieties with good reduction).
items.note: Proof by induction on topological transcendence degree through points of types (2)–(4), with de Jong's alterations; cf. the coalesced Part II's 'good-reduction-generated rigid motives'.

items.name: Proposition 10.3 (= Theorem 1.12, relative case): rigidity of D_mot
items.statement: For A analytic of finite cohomological dimension, D_mot(M_arc(A)) is rigid (Gaitsgory–Rozenblyum's notion); more generally for qcqs arc-sheaves X of finite cohomological dimension whose points are reached by quasi-pro-étale maps from geometric points. Proof: ℤ_mot[U] → ℤ_mot[V] is compact for U ⋐ V ⊂ 𝔸ⁿ_X (compactly assembled), and generation by sequential colimits along trace-class maps (Ramzi [Ram24b, Cor. 4.57]). Mixed Tate motives D_MT(X) (geometric fibres generated by the ℤ(n), Definition 10.7) form an arc-sheaf of categories (Proposition 10.8), are generated by the ℤ(n) over strictly totally disconnected X (Proposition 10.9) and are rigid (Proposition 10.10).
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.12, pp. 6–7; §10, Proposition 10.3, Definition 10.7, Propositions 10.8–10.10, pp. 54–57
items.note: Unlike étale sheaves on schemes or rigid spaces, where compact objects need not be dualizable.

items.name: Lemma 10.4 and Corollary 10.6: quasi-pro-étale descent and Künneth
items.statement: For quasi-pro-étale proper f : Y → X, D_mot(Y) ≅ Mod_{f_*ℤ}(D_mot(X)) (Barr–Beck–Lurie), and D_mot of a cofiltered limit of such is the colimit (Lemma 10.4); for qcqs X → S ← Y as in Proposition 10.3, D_mot(X) ⊗_{D_mot(S)} D_mot(Y) → D_mot(X ×_S Y) is fully faithful (Corollary 10.6).

items.name: ∞-categorical inputs: dualizable, compactly assembled and rigid categories
items.statement: Presentable stable ∞-categories that are compactly assembled (colim : Ind(C) → C has a left adjoint; Ramzi [Ram24a, Thm 2.39]) are exactly the dualizable ones; rigid symmetric monoidal categories (Gaitsgory–Rozenblyum [GR17, I.9.1.2]) and their characterisation by generation along trace-class maps (Ramzi [Ram24b]); relative tensor products of rigid categories are rigid; adjoining a ⊗-inverse of a symmetric object (Robalo); symmetric monoidal Verdier quotients by ⊗-ideals (Nikolaus–Scholze [NS18, Thm I.3.6]); Barr–Beck–Lurie; descendable algebras (Mathew [Mat16, Def. 3.18]).
items.note: EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:presentability plans Ind-completion, compact objects and extension of exact functors for the shared enhancement; dualizable and rigid presentable categories belong there.

items.name: Theorem 11.1 (= Proposition 1.13): D_mot(k) is Voevodsky's category of étale motives
items.statement: For an algebraically closed discrete field k, D_mot(k) is generated by the compact dualizable ℤ_mot[X](−j), X smooth projective, j ∈ ℤ; Hom(ℤ_mot[X](−j), ℤ) is rationally the weight-j Adams piece of K(X) and, profinitely (prime to p), pro-étale cohomology with Ẑ_{p′}(j). Hence the comparison functor from Voevodsky's étale motives (étale descent, 𝔸¹-invariance, G_m-stability) is an equivalence (Remark 11.2).
items.note: Proof through K = k((T))_{1/2}: f_♯ exists and f_♯ℤ = (f_*ℤ)^∨ splits off ℤ; K(X_C)_ℚ via excision on regular schemes.

items.name: Voevodsky's category of étale motives over a field
items.statement: The presentable stable ∞-category of étale motives over a field k: generated by smooth k-schemes, subject to étale descent, 𝔸¹-invariance and G_m-stability, with cancellation and rational Hom groups governed by K-theory.
items.note: MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.4 plans geometric mixed motives with A¹-invariance and Tate stabilisation, and MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5a finite correspondences, effective motivic complexes and cancellation.

items.name: Definition 11.3 and Proposition 11.4: motivic nearby cycles
items.statement: For C the completed algebraic closure of k((T))_{1/2} and f : M_arc(C) → M_arc(k), D_mot(C) = Mod_{f_*ℤ}(D_mot(k)); a pseudouniformiser π with compatible roots π^{1/n} (n prime to p) gives f_*ℤ ≅ g_*ℤ → ℤ (g : G̃_m,k → M_arc(k), G̃_m = lim G_m), and Ψ = Ψ(π^{1/n}) : D_mot(C) → D_mot(k) is base change along it (Definition 11.3); f_*ℤ → ℤ is descendable, so Ψ is conservative ('neutral Tannakian', Proposition 11.4).
items.note: The coalesced Part II carries 'Chosen augmentation and motivic nearby cycles' for RigDA (Binda–Kato–Vezzani, BGV).

items.name: Propositions 11.5–11.8: mixed Tate motives over 𝔽̄_p and the motivic t-structure
items.statement: Let MG_k be the stack over ℤ[1/p] of line bundles L with compatible L/n ≅ μ_n(k) ⊗ R (≅ BG_m^rat, G_m^rat = Spec(ℚ[T^{±1}] ×_ℚ ℤ[1/p])); D_qc(MG_k) is compactly generated by L^{⊗n}, and D_qc(MG_k) → D_mot(k) is fully faithful with image D_MT(k), the subcategory generated by the ℤ(n) (Proposition 11.6), giving the motivic t-structure on D_MT(k); D_MT(C) ⊗_{D_MT(k)} D_mot(k) ≅ D_mot(C) (Proposition 11.7); Ψ : D_MT(C) → D_MT(k) is conservative, t-exact and symmetric monoidal (Proposition 11.8).

items.name: Theorem 11.9 and Corollary 11.10 (= Theorem 1.14): motives over C by monodromy
items.statement: The gerbe MG_C → MG_k banded by Hom(ℚ, L) gives D_qc(MG_C) ≅ D_MT(C) and D_mot(C) ≅ D_mot(k) ⊗_{D_qc(MG_k)} D_qc(MG_C) (Theorem 11.9); a choice of π^{1/n} makes Ψ a symmetric monoidal equivalence D_mot(C) ≅ {(A, N) : A ∈ D_mot(k), N : A → A ⊗ ℚ(−1) locally nilpotent}, and rationally the choice of π suffices (Corollary 11.10).
items.note: Previously proved rationally by Binda–Gallauer–Vezzani [BGV23]; the coalesced Part II imports BGV for its log-free comparison.

items.name: Proposition 12.1 and Corollary 12.2: arc-stacks as partially proper v-stacks
items.statement: In characteristic p, with N → ∗ the v-sheaf of norms (an ℝ_{>0}-torsor), the functors (R, R⁺) ↦ R and R ↦ (R, (𝔽_p + R°°)~) induce adjoint morphisms of topoi a^* : vStack/N → arcStack, b^* : arcStack → vStack/N with (b^*Y)(R, R⁺) = Y(R), and b^*a^*X the canonical compactification [Sch17, Prop. 18.6] (Proposition 12.1); b^* is fully faithful onto the partially proper v-stacks (Corollary 12.2). A variant arcStack′ on perfectoid Tate 𝔽_p-algebras (the arc-topology on Huber pairs) removes N.
items.note: Imports DiamondsAndVStacks (v-stacks, canonical compactifications) rather than re-planning them.

items.name: Propositions 12.3–12.4: torsion motives and overconvergent étale sheaves on diamonds
items.statement: For a small v-stack X with Y = a′^*X and n prime to p, D_mot(Y, ℤ/n) ≅ D_et(Y, ℤ/n) ↪ D_et(X, ℤ/n) is fully faithful onto overconvergent étale sheaves, compatibly with pullback, tensor products and proper pushforward of finite cohomological dimension (Proposition 12.3, via [Sch17, Props 13.13, 22.7]); for a spatial diamond of finite cohomological dimension the inclusion has a colimit-preserving right adjoint, D_et(X, ℤ/n) being compactly generated (Proposition 12.4).
items.note: Imports DiamondEtaleCohomology's D_et of diamonds; this is the bridge to the companion 'Geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence, motivically' (independence of ℓ, Fargues–Scholze Conjecture I.9.5).

items.name: Proposition 1.5: effective motives over a geometric point
items.statement: For X = M_arc(C), C algebraically closed non-discrete: (i) C = ℂ: D(ℤ) ≅ D^eff_mot(X), the finitary sheaves; (ii) C nonarchimedean, n invertible in the residue field: D(ℤ/n) ≅ D^eff_mot(X, ℤ/n), ball-invariance ⇔ invariance under change of algebraically closed field; (iii) residue characteristic p: p is invertible in D^eff_mot(X); (iv) mixed characteristic: tilting gives D^eff_mot(C) ≅ D^eff_mot(C^♭). So only ℚ-coefficients over nonarchimedean fields are new.
items.note: Assembled from Theorem 4.14, Proposition 5.9, Corollary 6.6, Theorem 6.7 and Proposition 6.8.
